spots.s: 83 acres on the Sound: paved loop for a sunset walk, a sandy beach, and the Cove Island Wildlife Sanctuary boardwalk for birding at dawn.
Downtown's dinner-and-drinks strip: tree-lined blocks of restaurants, cocktail bars and patios a short walk from the Palace Theatre.
Shippan's big waterfront park: beach, boardwalk and a public fishing pier; the hillside doubles as the city's best sledding run after a snow.
Stamford's restored 1927 vaudeville house: touring concerts, comedy, Broadway tours and Orchestra Lumos — dinner on Bedford St first.
Downtown's central park: riverside paths, a 1916-style wooden carousel, cherry blossoms in April and the outdoor Cohen skating rink in winter.
Stroll the marina boardwalk past the yachts and the Commons, then grab dinner or drinks on the water — Stamford's easiest waterfront date.
South Norwalk's historic brick strip: bars, restaurants and live music along Washington St, steps from the aquarium and the river.
118 acres on the north side: a working heritage farm, art galleries in a stone Tudor mansion, an observatory and woodland trails.
Long Island Sound's own sea life — sharks, seals, river otters and jellies — on the water in SoNo; pair it with dinner on Washington St.
1860s Second Empire mansion with lavish stenciled interiors; guided tours and a festive holiday-season dress-up.
91 acres of champion trees, gardens and woodland trails; quiet, free-feeling and great for a fall-foliage walk.
Philip Johnson's 1949 glass pavilion and 49-acre estate; guided tours by reservation from the Elm St visitor center, season runs April to mid-December.
Norwalk's town beach and pier: long sunset views over the Norwalk Islands, kayak launch, and a waterfront stroll to Shady Beach.
147-acre peninsula with beaches, a causeway loop and Manhattan skyline views; pass required May–Oct, open to all Nov–Apr.
Artists' colony in the woods since 1922: free galleries, classes and openings at the Silvermine Guild.
Greenwich's expanded art-and-science museum: rotating major exhibitions, American paintings and a natural-history wing next to Bruce Park.
A mile of boutiques, cafés and restaurants from the train station to the Post Road; strolls best on a Saturday or under the holiday lights.
Westport's classic town beach: the cannons, the boardwalk and a long sunset walk out toward Sherwood Island.
A converted 1830s barn turned summer-stock legend; intimate plays, concerts and the holiday show.
Connecticut's first state park: 1.5 miles of beach, salt marsh trails and a nature center; off-season it's an empty-beach walk with big Sound views.
Port Chester's ornate 1926 rock palace — one of the best-sounding rooms in the region; catch a late set in Garcia's bar next door.
Free weekend walks among 45 sculptures (Calder, Moore, Rodin) on PepsiCo's manicured HQ grounds; 2026 season ends Nov 22.
1928 Art Deco amusement park on the Sound with the wooden Dragon Coaster, boardwalk and beach; seasonal, May to Labor Day.
The painter J. Alden Weir's farm and studio — Connecticut's only national park; walk the pond loop and the stone walls he painted.
500-seat hall where big names play small: singer-songwriters, comedy and holiday concerts in a pretty New England town.
The state's only zoo: Amur tigers, red wolves and a rainforest building, plus a vintage carousel.

events.s: Santa, Rudolph and the Grinch rappel 22 stories down Landmark Square, then fireworks and a march up Bedford St to light the tree in Latham Park.
Watch the parade's giant balloons come to life on Hoyt St, with live music, performances and Santa.
Soft-rock duo's 'A Matter of Time' tour at the Palace — a nostalgic date night.
Michael Stern conducts Berlioz's Symphonie fantastique plus overtures by Mayer and Farrenc and Ortiz's Tzam at the Palace.
'Crimson and Clover' and 'Mony Mony' live at the Palace.
The percussion phenomenon — trash cans, brooms and pure rhythm — for one night at the Palace.
The holiday classic at the Palace — matinee and evening shows both days.
Touring Nutcracker with a live orchestra at the Palace during the holiday week.
One of the country's largest balloon parades — giant helium balloons, marching bands and dance troupes through downtown the Sunday before Thanksgiving.
Yellin's monumental layered-glass sculptures at the Bruce Museum.

events.n: A Great Breach in Nature: J Henry Fair
events.s: Striking aerial photographs of industrial landscapes by J Henry Fair at the Bruce Museum.

events.n: Christine Ebersole: Home for the Holidays
events.s: The Tony winner sings holiday standards with Billy Stritch at the piano at Westport Country Playhouse.
Holmes investigates the death of Ebenezer Scrooge in this Dickens-meets-Doyle holiday mystery at Westport Country Playhouse.
The comic and screenwriter's tour stop at the Capitol Theatre.
The Machine brings his party-hard stand-up to the Capitol Theatre.
Phish's frontman in Garcia's, the Capitol Theatre's small bar room — a rare up-close night.
Vermont jam band's three-night Thanksgiving-weekend run at the Capitol Theatre.
John Bonham's son leads a full-throttle Zeppelin set at the Capitol Theatre.
Devon Allman and Duane Betts' all-star Allman Brothers celebration, 'A Decade of Revival', at the Capitol.
Warren Haynes' band warms up its New Year's run with two nights at the Capitol, Audley Freed sitting in.
Fairfield men's hoops hosts Navy and Central Connecticut over Thanksgiving weekend at Mahoney Arena.
Fairfield men's basketball opens Metro Conference play against Manhattan at Mahoney Arena.

events.n: Michelle Wolf: Best Job in the World
events.s: The sharp-tongued stand-up brings her new hour to the Ridgefield Playhouse.

events.n: John C. Reilly is Mister Romantic
events.s: The actor's old-time song-and-story show of love ballads at the Ridgefield Playhouse.
The singer-songwriter's intimate solo-style show at the Ridgefield Playhouse.

events.n: Judy Collins: Sweet Judy Blue Eyes Farewell
events.s: The folk legend's farewell tour, two nights at the Ridgefield Playhouse.

events.n: Old Crow Medicine Show: Holiday Hootenanny
events.s: The string band's rowdy holiday show at the Ridgefield Playhouse.
The Grammy-nominated singer's soulful holiday show at the Ridgefield Playhouse.

nightlife.s: Restored 1926 movie palace on the CT line where jam bands, hip-hop and R&B tours play under a giant light-show dome; grab a drink in the lobby bars before the headliner.
The Capitol's intimate side room and bar, entered just right of the main doors: tribute nights, funk and soul bands, and after-shows that run late on concert nights.
The old Wall Street Theater in Norwalk, reborn under the College Street Music Hall team: national touring acts, dance parties and Bingo Loco nights in a restored vintage theater.
Black Rock's bar-and-stage room: soul, funk, Latin and rock bands on the calendar, plus a weekend brunch. Easy pre-show dinner on Fairfield Ave.
225-seat black box in downtown Fairfield where every seat is close: singer-songwriters, jazz and blues acts; walk to dinner on Post Rd after.
Westchester's only dedicated jazz club: an intimate 90-seat room by the Tarrytown station with weekend sets by NYC players. Book a table up front.
Thursday-night jazz at Westport's VFW Post 399, run by the Jazz Society of Fairfield County: NYC players, a small cover that goes to the band, and dinner if you reserve.
The Manhattan club's 250-seat Stamford outpost by the Town Center: headliners and stacked showcases Wed–Sat, then walk to the Bedford St bars.
Downtown Bridgeport's big comedy room, booking national names like Tony Rock and Russell Peters on two-show weekend nights.
Harbor Point's big rooftop bar with water views and a lively downstairs bar; open to 2am Fri–Sat, with heated igloos on the roof in winter.
Eighth-floor seasonal rooftop atop the Residence Inn, roughly May–Oct: sunset cocktails over the Norwalk River and SoNo rooftops. Reserve for weekend evenings.
Find the 'Global Entry Passport Photos' door in the alley off N Main, press the button and the wall slides open. Order the smoked dirty martini or Hell's Kitchen. Rooftop upstairs in season.
Craft cocktail lounge down Donnelly Walk, an alley behind Archie Moore's. Get the lavender martini or the Smokeshow (mezcal + bourbon), or a gin bowl for the group.
Canal St cantina that becomes a dance floor on weekends: DJs spinning reggaeton, bachata, kompa and afrobeats until 2, plus R&B party nights. 21+ after 9pm.
Downtown Stamford club booking reggaeton and dembow headliners (Jory Boy, El Cherry Scom in fall 2026). Check its socials for this weekend's show.
Monthly Sunday-afternoon house and EDM party in the Annex level of the Stamford Town Center garage, from 2pm. OMNOM and Laidback Luke opened the 2026 run; dates on its Instagram.
Yonkers Raceway's slots-and-electronic-tables casino, open late every day, with harness racing out back. The closest casino floor, down the Hutch.

eats.s: Ten-seat counter with a 16-course omakase only, seatings at 5, 7 and 9pm five nights a week. Chef Edwin came from Sushi of Gari and Nobu. Reservations required.
Book the long blond counter in the omakase room for 12 or 15 courses: bluefin belly with caviar, kinmedai, shima-aji. Get the toro toast à la carte. Weekday lunch is calmest.
Chef Rio Yonathan's tiny BYOB counter in Old Greenwich. Ask for the $135 omakase at the bar (Tue–Sat); don't miss the chutoro with seared foie gras or the uni chawanmushi.
The area's value omakase: 15 courses for about $68 (ten nigiri, a hand roll, tamago, miso), from the team behind Ginkgo Sichuan. Small room, so go early.
Downtown Stamford's sushi lounge and sake bar on Summer St. Sit at the counter for nigiri, or ask what's off-menu that night.
Two rooms from chef Jeff Taibe: a loud front izakaya for yakitori, karaage and ramen, and a back temaki-ya for DIY hand rolls like Hokkaido scallop.
New in 2026 in Riverside: crisp-nori hand rolls handed across the bar one at a time, plus ramen and noodle bowls. A fun quick date before a movie.
Stamford's first ramen shop, on Bedford's restaurant row: order the tonkotsu miso for the deepest broth, plus a karaage bao.
Connecticut-born noodle bar with a sidewalk patio on Bedford St: tonkotsu ramen, pho, KFC bao and good cocktails. Reliable late weeknight dinner.
Built-in tabletop grills in a rustic Scarsdale room near the station. Galbi and pork belly come with house banchan and dipping sauces. Call ahead for a grill table.
No-frills White Plains Korean on Central Ave: marinated kalbi, galbi-tang short-rib soup, the dish regulars rave about.
Tiny, long-loved Darien Thai counter by the train. Get the laksa, drunken noodles or green curry, then take a walk on the Post Rd.
Stamford's 1935 bar-pie original: cracker-thin pizza, no slices, no menu fuss. Order the stinger (hot oil + hot cherry peppers) with sausage, and a cold beer at the bar.
New Haven's coal-fired legend on High Ridge Rd, no I-95 trip needed. Order the white clam pie, made only with fresh-shucked littlenecks, and a Foxon Park birch beer.
Waterside seafood house on the Five Mile River, with boats tied up at the dock. Get the warm butter-poached CT lobster roll at sunset; valet is the easy way to park.

chinese.n: Nan Xiang Xiao Long Bao 南翔小笼包
chinese.s: Flushing's Michelin-listed Shanghainese dumpling house, now by the Stamford Town Center. Walk-in only. Order the Lucky Six sampler, pan-fried pork buns and braised beef noodle soup.

chinese.n: Yi Fang Taiwan Fruit Tea 一芳
chinese.s: Connecticut's first Yi Fang, on Columbus Park: the signature pineapple-jam fruit tea over cold-brewed Taiwanese oolong, or brown sugar oolong with boba.
Greenwich Ave's polished Chinese dining room with a weekend dim sum brunch; its Lunar New Year brunch brings a lion dance.
Fairfield's real-deal Sichuan, serving full málà since 2017. Get the sole and tofu in chili broth, cumin lamb, chicken dry pot and tea-smoked duck. Order Peking duck 2 hours ahead.

chinese.n: Aberdeen Seafood & Dim Sum 点心
chinese.s: Westchester's classic Cantonese dim sum hall, off the Marriott lobby: har gow, pork siu mai and mini pork buns daily except Tuesday. Arrive at opening on weekends.
Michelin inspectors' favorite, full of multi-generation family tables. Get the Mandarin pork shank, wild-pepper shrimp, soup dumplings and the prime-rib hot pot. Book a booth.
The nearest big pan-Asian supermarket: live seafood, thin-sliced hot pot meats, Sichuan peppercorns and doubanjiang, frozen dumplings and Chinese snacks by the aisle.

chinese.n: Old Street Dim Sum & Hot Pot 火锅
chinese.s: Every table has its own burner: pick broths and pile in ingredients. Dim sum all day, plus hot-oil dumplings and diced rabbit with peanuts. Big round hot pot table for groups.
The Chicago Sichuan group's Milford outpost (Ginkgo's sister). Go for the ma-la chef's specials, dan dan noodles and spicy beef noodle soup.
The NYC northern-Chinese noodle shop's New Haven branch in Ninth Square. Watch the noodles get pulled to order, and get them in beef soup or stir-fried with the Michelin-noted dumplings.

Yale-China's annual Lunar New Year festival, Connecticut's largest: a lion-dance parade from the Shops at Yale, then workshops and performances downtown. The 2027 Year of the Goat date isn't announced yet.

fishing.s: Stamford's city pier on the Sound off Shippan Ave: scup, sea robins, snapper blues in late summer, stripers at dusk. Summer parking needs a permit (May–Sep); open lot in the off-season. CT marine license required.
Rocky points and seawall at the mouth of Holly Pond: stripers and blues on moving water at dawn and dusk, porgies in summer. Nonresident day pass sold at the gate in season.

Greenwich's peninsula park, ringed by rocky points that hold fall stripers and blues. Resident pass only in season, but entry is free for everyone Nov 1–Apr 30, which happens to be the late-run striper window.

fishing.n: Calf Pasture Beach – Capt. William Clark Fishing Pier
fishing.s: Norwalk's fishing pier at the harbor mouth: summer porgies, fluke and blowfish, plus stripers on the evening tide. There's also a small unpaved ramp for cartop boats.

Westport state park. DEEP lists blackfish, bluefish, scup, both flounders and stripers off Sherwood Point and the East and West jetties (Apr 15–Sep 30). Off-season the whole beach is open 8a–sunset. Free parking with CT plates.

A rock-and-sand bar running about a mile out from Fairfield that you can walk on the falling tide. Fly and spin anglers cast to stripers and blues holding in the rips. Watch the incoming tide: it cuts you off. Park at Veterans Park on Reef Rd.

Private 4- and 6-hour trips out of Stamford Harbor, May–Oct, with Capt. Lou Cavaliere, who has fished the Sound since 1975. Targets stripers, blues, porgy, sea bass and tautog, with a 4–5 week false albacore run in fall.

DEEP Trout Management Area in Greenwich and Stamford. Trout of 9 inches or more may be kept from the 2nd Sat in April through Aug 31; the rest of the year is catch-and-release. Heavily stocked and close to town. Trout stamp required.

DEEP fly-fishing-only stretch from Dorr's Mill Dam down to the Merritt Pkwy in Westport (the Doc Skerlick area off Ford Rd). Stocked browns and rainbows on easy riffles, a good place to learn. Trout stamp required.

Tidal water below the dam where stripers stack up all winter, then feed on staging herring in spring. DEEP leases a fishing site on the Derby side; marine rules apply, so there is effectively no closed season.

About 1½ miles of cold tailwater between the East Branch and Diverting reservoirs near Brewster. NY DEC stocked about 7,400 browns and rainbows in spring 2026, and it fishes year-round. NY license required; check DEC regs for the special section.

Connecticut's biggest lake at 5,064 acres and a top tournament bass water, with largemouth, smallmouth, trout and panfish. DEEP's year-round concrete ramp has about 50 spaces. Launch early, because boat traffic gets heavy.

biking.s: Downtown Stamford's paved riverwalk through a restored river park, with cherry blossoms in spring. It's short and fully paved, a coffee cruise rather than a trail ride. The greenway is slowly being extended toward the harbor.

~10 mi of tight singletrack and fire roads straddling the Stamford/Greenwich line, incl. NEMBA's 'Mianus Maze' loop. Rocky technical bits plus easy doubletrack; shared with hikers and dogs. The red-barn lot fills early on weekends.

biking.n: Norwalk River Valley Trail – Wilton Loop
biking.s: A 6.2-mi loop: stone-dust path and boardwalk through the river woods on the east side, road shoulders on the west. Easy gravel-bike or family ride, not MTB terrain. Take care on Skunk Ln.
Aspetuck Land Trust preserve with 1,000+ acres of XC singletrack, flowy to very technical. Bikes May 1–Dec 31 only, on marked trails (orchard closed), and not when wet. Main lot on Bradley Rd.

431 acres of tight, hilly singletrack in Mount Pleasant, with about 5 mi of trails aimed at experienced riders and newer jump/skills lines by the lot. Open 8a–dusk year-round, and reachable from Pleasantville Metro-North.

1,017-acre state park in Redding with gravel carriage roads, ponds and rooty, technical singletrack. A few marked trails are foot-only. Free, open 8a–sunset. Archery deer season runs Sep 15–Dec 31, so wear orange.

Short punchy climbs but some of the most technical riding near the city, with log piles, slickrock and drops on 278 wooded acres in Yonkers. Bring pads. No e-bikes, and trails can close after heavy rain.

Westchester's flagship riding: 20+ mi of color-coded trails on 1,538 acres outside Peekskill, from beginner loops to rock gardens and descents. No e-bikes. Parking is $5–10 on summer and weekend days.

Trumbull's XC and freeride playground (aka Old Mine Park): about 15 miles of marked singletrack along the Pequonnock, drops from 2 to 20 ft and the 30-ft Green Monster roller, with a rail trail north for an epic.
Rugged, very technical Newtown singletrack along Lake Zoar from the boat ramp — it gets harder past the 'Kissing Oaks' — looping back on forest road, with plenty of unmarked trail to explore.

social.n: Stamford Board Games Group – Chelsea Piers
social.s: A 2,300-member Meetup group that fills the upstairs bar at Chelsea Piers with lighter and intro games. Dinner around 6, games from about 6:30. Free.
The same group's heavier night, for longer and more complex games plus crokinole, at the Glenbrook Athletic Club lodge.
A Saturday market in Veterans Memorial Park with local produce, flowers, bread, cheese and jams. Free yoga at 9 and live music 10:30–12:30. Takes SNAP/WIC, and market parking is free.
A downtown pub quiz with MC JHype, free to play. Teams form at the bar, so it's easy to get absorbed into one.

A free weekly group run founded in 2024 that grew fast enough to host Stamford's first half marathon in 30+ years (Apr 2026). All paces, with walking options. The start point rotates, so check @stamford.runclub.

social.n: Trivia Tuesday at Bareburger Harbor Point
social.s: Let's Go Trivia hosts weekly trivia at the Harbor Point Bareburger, with dates posted into 2027. A waterfront-neighborhood crowd of young residents.
The club's weekend group run from the Old Greenwich firehouse, all levels welcome, with a 7:45a walk group alongside. Weekday runs leave from the Greenwich Y (Mon 6p, Wed 6:30a, Thu evening).
Greenwich's long-running Saturday market in the Horseneck commuter lot: farm stands, local catch, bakers. The 2026 season runs to Nov 21.
Unscripted Spanish conversation, not a class, for intermediate and up. The library runs Italian, French, German and Japanese tables too. Email the organizers before your first visit.

One of the county's best markets: outdoors at the Imperial Ave lot May–early Nov, then indoors in Gilbertie's heated greenhouses at 7 Sylvan Ln through mid-March (2025–26 pattern; confirm winter dates).

skiing.s: The closest lifts to Stamford: ~500-ft vertical (listings vary 400–600), 22 trails, 3 chairs + 4 carpets, 100% snowmaking, open till 9p every night. Small, but a weeknight after-work run is realistic.
Bergen County park hill: 274-ft vertical, 12 trails, 100% snowmaking, ~80% lit for night skiing, plus 15–17 tubing lanes ~800 ft long. Best for first-timers and a tubing night, not for mileage.
Warwick's family hill: ~450-ft vertical, 13 trails, 3 chairs, 100% snowmaking, night skiing Tue–Sat (80% lit), and a 600-ft tubing run that sells out on weekends — book tubing online ahead.
425-ft vertical, 14 trails, 100% snowmaking, every trail and lift lit: nights Mon–Thu 5–9p and Fri–Sat 5–10p, plus terrain parks. Straight up I-84 — the easiest CT night session.
Middlefield hill with 417-ft vertical, 19 trails, ~85% snowmaking (68 of 80 acres), night skiing on 40 acres off 6 lifts, and a snow-tubing park. A solid CT family night out.
New Jersey's big one: 1,040-ft vertical, 46 trails across four peaks, night skiing on most terrain and 16 terrain parks. The most vertical within ~75 minutes — and the park scene to match.
Connecticut's most terrain: 650-ft vertical, 27 trails on 112 acres, 100% snowmaking, night skiing 6 nights on 16 trails. Snowmaking was invented here — the classic Litchfield Hills day.
625-ft vertical, 17 trails, 100% snowmaking, two terrain parks, and night skiing till 10p every night on 16 lit trails — regroomed at 6p. The go-to CT night session.
Revived Catskills hill: 400-ft vertical, and 20 trails for 2026–27 as the North Pod reopens with a triple chair, new lights for night skiing and Free Bird, a 43° double black. Plans to open Dec 19.
1,000-ft vertical on the NY–MA line, 44 trails, 93% snowmaking, night skiing on 22 trails Wed–Sat (late Dec–early Mar). A real-mountain vertical you can still ski under the lights.
Great Barrington's cruiser mountain: 1,000-ft vertical, 22 trails, 100% snowmaking, five quads (incl. new Jane's Quad), terrain parks and tubing. Wide, well-groomed blues — the easy Berkshires day.
Old-school Berkshires hill (opened 1947, owned by Butternut since 2016): 400-ft vertical, ~15 trails, a double chair and T-bar, near-full snowmaking, night skiing Wed–Sun 4–9p. Cheap and uncrowded.
Independent Poconos mountain: 700-ft vertical, 23 trails, 100% snowmaking, night skiing on most trails, plus a tubing park. Known for aggressive snowmaking and grooming — an easy I-80 day.
The real-mountain day trip: 1,600-ft vertical, 67 trails, 320 acres, 13 lifts, and the self-styled snowmaking capital of the world. The full-size Catskills day; no night skiing.
State-run Catskills mountain: 1,404-ft vertical, 62 trails incl. glades and parks, 171 acres, 96% snowmaking, gondola, and a 2.3-mile longest run. Pick it for long cruising runs.
1,600-ft vertical, 60 trails, 12 lifts, ~97% snowmaking, six terrain parks. Now a semi-private club, but public day tickets are still sold online; quantities have been limited, so buy ahead.
Birthplace of night skiing (GE floodlights, 1936): 750-ft vertical, ~22 trails, night skiing Mon–Sat, tubing Thu–Sun, a terrain park. Pittsfield's rebuilt local mountain, now in its 95th season.
The Poconos' big resort: 800-ft vertical, 46 trails, 100% snowmaking, night skiing on 160 of 166 acres, 3 terrain parks and 40+ snow-tubing lanes with glow-lit night tubing.

remote.s: Harbor Point worklounge at 700 Canal St. High-speed Wi-Fi, focus room and private phone rooms, coffee, tea & fruit water, free surface parking and a shuttle to Stamford station (5 min). Unlimited members get 7a–7p access, 150 prints/mo, 4 hr of meeting-room credit and drop-ins at 20+ Serendipity Labs nationwide. Day pass is M–F 8:30a–5p.
remote.b: Plenty of room and privacy, per members; groups sometimes book it for the day

remote.s: Waterfront coworking at 290 Harbor Dr on the Shippan peninsula, open 24/7. High-speed Wi-Fi, privacy booths, kitchen, gym, a studio, lockable filing cabinets, mail handling and on-site parking, plus member socials and pro events.

Community-first coworking at 320 Post Rd, downtown Darien. Coffee, tea & snacks, conference rooms, a podcast room, a fitness center, printing, a business address and 24/7 member access; monthly meetups and networking nights. Day passes are weekday 9a–5p at an open desk.
remote.b: Private-office day passes can sell out; book at least 24 hours ahead

remote.s: HAYVN's second space, at 1700 E Putnam Ave in Old Greenwich. Same playbook as Darien: open desks, coffee, Wi-Fi, printing and free parking on a day pass (weekdays 9a–5p), plus conference rooms, a podcast room and 24/7 access for members.
remote.p: Day pass from $50 · private office day $150

remote.s: The biggest Regus downtown, at 263 Tresser Blvd across from the Stamford Town Center — book an hour, half-day or day in the Regus app. Wi-Fi, staffed reception, meeting rooms by the hour and access to Regus' global network on a membership. Sister centers at 20 Summer St (day office from $49) and Soundview.

Private-office center on the 4th floor of 6 Landmark Square, a block from the train. Not a hot-desk room: it's day offices and hourly meeting rooms with free coffee & tea, A/V, whiteboards, printer, kitchen and outdoor space. M–F 8:30a–5p.
remote.p: Meeting room from $20/hr · day office from $230 · office from $800/mo
remote.b: Quiet and private, per a member review

remote.s: Stamford's main library at Broad & Bedford, downtown. Free Wi-Fi, reservable study rooms and solo booths on the 2nd and 3rd floors (one 120-min slot a day, book a day ahead), public computers, printing & fax, and Winfield Street Coffee in the building. Sun 1–5, Mon–Thu 10–8, Sat 10–5; closed Fri.
remote.b: Quiet work areas; few study rooms, booked a day ahead, one 2-hour slot a day

remote.s: One of the best libraries in the state, at 1441 Post Rd. Wi-Fi reaches out into the courtyard, a café on the main level, silent study rooms for two on the mezzanine, talk-friendly study pods upstairs and group rooms for up to 8 (non-residents can book same-day online). Non-residents get a computer day pass at the 2nd-floor desk. Mon–Thu 9–9, Fri 9–6, Sat–Sun 11–5.
remote.b: Among CT's busiest (1,300 visits a day); study rooms in high demand at finals

remote.s: Main library at 101 W Putnam Ave. Free Wi-Fi, free individual and group study rooms (up to 3 hr a day), private phone booths for calls, scanners, copiers and wireless printing. Mon–Fri 9–9, Sat 9–5, Sun 1–5. The in-house café has been temporarily closed, so bring a coffee.
remote.b: Quiet study areas throughout; not crowded on Saturdays, per a review

remote.s: Small, quiet indie coffeehouse at 575 Hope St in Springdale: fast free Wi-Fi, a window desk, a few tables and a couch corner, espresso and baked goods. Seats go early — it's a short-session spot, not an all-day office.
remote.b: Small shop; weekends get busy, weekdays calmer; parking tight at peak

remote.s: Café at 20 Grove St in downtown Darien, Moffly Media's top pick for escaping the home office: a café hum and soft music, busy but not loud, with fresh coffee and pastries. Go mid-morning, when the crowds thin. Opens 7a weekdays and 8a weekends, and closes mid-afternoon.
remote.b: Limited tables can fill with laptop users; courtyard seats add room

remote.s: 96 Broad St downtown, right beside the Ferguson Library, so the library's free desks are next door when you need quiet. Wi-Fi, laptops welcome and abundant seating in a bright room with a plant wall. Pastries, sandwiches and salads. Open Mon–Sat 7a–5p, Sun 7a–4p.
remote.b: Single espresso machine strains at busy hours; ample seating
